comment: Cite contents properly throughout the manuscript.
response: We rebuilt the bibliography from inspected primary records (journal/DOI records checked against Crossref, arXiv and the Hugging Face model card), cite the journal version of EuroSAT, add sources for the new methods (MAE pooling, HLS, AOPC), distinguish preprints from journal versions, and removed unsupported novelty and release claims. Every in-text key resolves and every bibliography entry is cited (checked by the manuscript gate). The legacy bibliography is preserved unchanged.
evidence: verified_sources.json (19 entries); manuscript_validation.json (citations_resolve, no_uncited_bibliography, verified_bibliography). Language proofreading by the authors is still required.

issue: RGB versus multispectral description and split provenance
experiment: Audit all 27,000 images, channels, class counts and duplicate hashes
response: We cite the EuroSAT journal paper and document the two local representations: 27,000 RGB JPEGs and the matching 13-band Sentinel-2 GeoTIFFs, their counts (18,900/4,050/4,050), classes, preprocessing, the random class-wise split, and the checks performed (file/pixel hashes, JPEG-GeoTIFF pairing). The upstream release version and geographic independence are unverified and stated as limitations. The empirical GeoTIFF band order (B8A stored last) is documented.

experiment: Deterministic metric and edge-case tests; real-data evaluation
response: We supplied formulas, inputs, ranges, directions, normalizations, edge cases and limitations. Macro-F1 is distinct from historical weighted F1. Calibration, uncertainty, stability, deletion faithfulness and representation are not treated as interchangeable.

issue: Overgeneralization beyond EuroSAT and experimental design
experiment: Match limitations to verified input and training audit
test: scope and discrepancy checks in manuscript validator
response: We rewrote the limitations: land-cover labels versus crop health, patch-level decisions, random non-geographic split, no real distribution shift, four architectures, five seeds that randomize only a linear head, frozen-backbone linear probing, different inputs/pretraining between the RGB and six-band cohorts, the apparent top-of-atmosphere versus surface-reflectance domain gap, masking artefacts in deletion, correlated components and subjective weights. Crop-health, disease and yield uses are future work.

experiment: Generate figures from validated prediction and explanation artifacts
test: figure hashes, source hashes and table consistency
response: All figures are regenerated from validated run records: accuracy with seed and bootstrap intervals, six components with intervals, reliability diagrams, deletion curves with random/least-salient controls, corruption curves, validation-versus-test training history, weight sensitivity, pairwise differences and confusion matrices. Each figure has a JSON sidecar with its plotted values and source hash; the legacy figures are not reused.
evidence: results/figures/manifest.json and sidecars; GeneratedAssetConsistencyTests; manuscript gate figure_* checks

issue: Missing contextual comparisons and exaggerated novelty
test: verified source registry and citation checks
response: We added a literature comparison covering EuroSAT, foundation models, XAI evaluation, calibration, corruption robustness and TorchGeo. Published scores are not pooled with local experiments. We explain protocol differences and limit the contribution to auditable integration.
evidence: docs/revision/LITERATURE_COMPARISON.md; verified_sources.json. Literature scores are not pooled with local runs; no external baseline was re-executed.

experiment: End-to-end real-data smoke run with saved artifacts
response: We documented and diagrammed the actual data, model, training, explanation, score and reporting path. The unified CLI uses tested components. Legacy prototypes are not represented as executed research; JSON and additive SQLite records preserve configurations, hashes, artifacts and failures.
evidence: docs/methodology.md; docs/revision/MODEL_INPUT_AUDIT.md; Section 3; tests; compliance report

comment: Compare the proposed work with published work.
issue: Need fair comparison with related research
experiment: Same targeted review as R1.6, with explicit fairness statement
response: We added the comparison and fairness paragraph, distinguish methodological literature from controlled same-protocol runs, and make no unexecuted baseline or superiority claim.

comment: Resolve Figure 7/Table 1 inconsistency: ResNet-18 test accuracy 91.53% versus validation accuracy around 84-86%.
issue: Unrecoverable epoch history and mixed legacy aggregation
experiment: Reconstruct Table I; compare both databases; re-execute the legacy trainer
response: We traced both numbers. Table 1 (91.53%) is the unweighted mean of all six stored ResNet-18 runs, three of one epoch and three of five epochs. Figure 7 (validation ~84-86%) matches a different execution of the same configuration: the reviewer-package copy of the database holds, under the identical run identifier, test accuracy 85.19% and final loss 0.499, whereas the main database holds 92.37% and 0.249 for that identifier, because the legacy store replaced metrics when a configuration was re-run. Re-executing the legacy trainer reproduced the main-database values exactly and not the figure, so the figure-like run cannot be regenerated. Both sources are preserved; the pooled table and the figure are withdrawn, and all results are replaced by a homogeneous five-seed, five-epoch cohort with validation and test accuracy plotted and labelled separately. The figure's own plotted data were not preserved, so its link to the earlier execution is strongly supported but not proven.

comment: Add standard deviations and 95% confidence intervals.
issue: Means lacked seed-level uncertainty and consistent replication
experiment: Homogeneous independent-seed groups; Student-t mean intervals
response: Every reported component, per model, has n=5 independent seeds, mean, sample SD, 95% Student-t interval and missing-run count (Tables [[tab:trust]] and [[tab:ci]]). Test-patch bootstrap intervals and paired comparisons are reported separately; the assumptions and the narrowness of seed intervals for a frozen backbone are stated. Intervals reflect no geographic variance.

experiment: Fixed-target noise stability and salient/random/least deletion curves
response: We renamed SSIM as explanation stability and implemented a separate deletion metric with a fixed target, explicit mean-RGB baseline, patch ordering and trapezoidal integration. Random and least-salient controls are retained. The new common attribution rule differs from legacy Grad-CAM and is explicitly documented.
evidence: explainability.py; tests ExplanationTests; results: stability SSIM and deletion AUC/AOPC with controls (Table [[tab:metrics]], Figure [[fig:deletion]])

comment: Clarify the composite score and Bayesian terminology.
issue: Weighted sum is not Bayesian inference; weighting sensitivity absent
experiment: Equal/default, alternative profiles and 50 deterministic perturbations
response: The score is a weighted sum T = sum w_j s_j with fixed, versioned weights (default 1/6 each) and fixed normalizations; it is renamed Composite Trust Score and explicitly not Bayesian or a probability. Sensitivity covers equal, reliability-priority and explanation-priority weights and 50 seeded perturbations, with scores, ranks, preferred models and Spearman correlations (Section [[sec:sensresults]]).

issue: Uncertainty and representation measures were not reported
experiment: Compute all six from saved predictions, deletion curves, corruptions and embeddings
response: All six components (macro-F1, 1-deletion AUC, 1-ECE, corrupted accuracy, 1-Brier/2, normalized silhouette) are computed for every model and seed and reported with intervals in Table [[tab:trust]] and Table [[tab:ci]]; the score rejects any missing or invalid component. Real geographic/seasonal OOD is not computed; the robustness component is a synthetic-corruption proxy and is labelled as such.
evidence: results/tables/table1.json; manuscript gate six_pillars_* checks; compliance metrics_valid

issue: Actual Prithvi checkpoint and adaptation were not used
response: The submitted "Prithvi-100M" was an RGB ViT-Base proxy (bit-identical metrics) and is withdrawn. The real Prithvi-EO-1.0-100M checkpoint (pinned revision, SHA-256 verified) is now evaluated. Adaptation: its six pretrained channels (HLS blue, green, red, narrow NIR, SWIR1, SWIR2) receive Sentinel-2 B02, B03, B04, B8A, B11, B12 from the GeoTIFFs (storage indices 1,2,3,12,10,11, verified empirically because the nominal order is wrong); no input parameter is added or initialized; one time step is used with a one-frame position embedding verified equal to the checkpoint's first frame; Prithvi's own normalization is used. Uncorrected domain differences (apparent top-of-atmosphere vs surface reflectance, 64->224 upsampling) are disclosed.

comment: Verify whether all models use the same spectral bands.
experiment: Input metadata and shape assertions for supported RGB architectures
response: We generated a model-input audit from the run records. The models do not use the same bands: ResNet-18, ViT-Base and ConvNeXt-T receive RGB; Prithvi receives six Sentinel-2 bands. All share the split and test patches. This is disclosed, cross-cohort comparisons are labelled confounded, and the weight analysis that includes all four models is marked descriptive. A controlled common-input comparison is not possible without an unvalidated input adapter (BLOCKED, stated as a limitation). Configuration, model metadata, tensor shape and registered representation are asserted on every run.

issue: Land-cover evidence does not validate crop disease or health
experiment: Claim audit against dataset labels and actual channels
response: Title kept. The abstract, introduction, methods, discussion, limitations and conclusion now describe EuroSAT land-cover classification, state that nothing here validates crop-health, disease or yield claims, and describe those as future work needing dedicated labels. The suggested "multispectral" wording is used only for the six-band Prithvi cohort; no 13-band experiment is claimed.
